_readme: Central code-factor register used by every tool. status: V = confirmed from a named source (search excerpt); C = standard clause content / recommended value, NA may differ; U = unverified typical value. Override any value in a PROJECT file (same structure, only the keys you change) and pass it with --factors project.json or env TENSILE_FACTORS=project.json. Run `python3 factors.py report` to list everything still unverified. Unverified (U) entries carry a 'range' used by --sensitivity checks: tools re-run the governing check at both ends and report whether the decision depends on the unverified value.

stress_factor_short.source: ASCE 55-10 'current industry practice' FS 4.0 for prestress + wind (ASCE 55-10 text) and general 4–5 practice (Birdair, literature)

stress_factor_long.source: ASCE 55-10 'current industry practice' FS 5.0 for prestress + snow; Birdair 'usually 5'. (P + D alone: 8.0, see fm159_PD)

fm159_PD.source: FM Global DS 1-59 (2021) Table 2.2.6.1, P+D, new-fabric strength

japan_long_divisor.source: MLIT Notification No. 666 (2002, amended 2007/2011), 第六 一 table, row (一) (no joint, or joint/weld width >= 40 mm; >= 75 mm for glass/PTFE class (一)): long-term allowable tensile stress = Fm/(80 t) N/mm2 with Fm in N/cm and t in mm, i.e. n_allow = Fm/8 per unit width. Fm = ministerially designated standard strength (第八). https://www.mlit.go.jp/notice/noticedata/pdf/201703/00006526.pdf

japan_short_divisor.source: MLIT Notification No. 666, 第六 一 table, row (一), membrane NOT folded (折りたたみを行わない場合): short-term = Fm/(40 t) -> Fm/4 per unit width. Same URL as japan_long_divisor

japan_short_divisor_folded.source: MLIT Notification No. 666, 第六 一 table, row (一), membrane folded (折りたたみを行う場合): short-term = Fm/(50 t) -> Fm/5 (long-term unchanged Fm/80t)

japan_long_divisor_narrow.source: MLIT Notification No. 666, 第六 一 table, row (二) (joint/weld narrower than 40 mm, or 75 mm for glass/PTFE): long-term Fm/(100 t) -> Fm/10

japan_short_divisor_narrow.source: MLIT Notification No. 666, 第六 一 table, row (二): short-term Fm/(50 t) -> Fm/5

japan_anchorage_long.source: MLIT Notification No. 666, 第六 二: allowable capacity of membrane anchorages (定着部) Fj/6 long-term, Fj = tensile strength from a test of the actual anchorage

japan_anchorage_short.source: MLIT Notification No. 666, 第六 二: anchorage Fj/3 short-term (第七 二: ultimate capacity also Fj/3)

seam_efficiency.source: PVC HF 0.80-0.90, PTFE heat-seal 0.70-0.80 (tensilecraft); JRC132615 (2023) Eurocode Outlook No. 5 (PES/PVC seam strength at 23 °C >= 90 % Types I-IV, >= 80 % Type V; at 70 °C >= 70/70/70/60/55 %) and No. 7 (glass/PTFE >= 80-90 % at 23 °C, >= 60-70 % at 70 °C). 0.8 is the lower value at 23 °C; use the seam test value

partial.source: German A-factor practice, JRC Science for Policy report JRC132615 (2023, re-edition of JRC100166 2016) 'Prospect for European Guidance for the Structural Design of Tensile Membrane Structures', Code Review No. 20 (DIN 4134 + Minte): 'fd = fk,23 / (γf · γM · Ai)', 'γM = 1.4 within the fabric surface, γM = 1.5 for connections', 'A0 = 1.0 – 1.2 (1.2)', 'A1 = 1.6 – 1.7 (1.5 – 3.4)', 'A2 = 1.1 – 1.2 (1.2)', 'A3 = 1.1 – 1.25 (1.4 – 1.95)' (brackets = connections); winter storm uses γM·A0·A2, maximum snow γM·A0·A1·A2, permanent γM·A0·A1·A2·A3. PES/PVC subtable = values inside these published ranges -> V. glass/PTFE and 'other' subtables are NOT from that source -> U (top-level status U because of them). NOT CEN/TS 19102 values (see ts19102)
partial.range_source: product A0·A1·A2·A3 over the JRC Code Review 20 fabric ranges relative to the PES/PVC table values (1.936 … 3.06 vs 2.47) = published material spread; the A-factors are material-specific test values

ts19102.source: CEN/TS 19102 format fd = fk,23/(γM·kbiax·kage·kdur·ktemp·ksize) with values 'modification factors according prCEN/TS 19102' for PES/PVC Type IV (Sattler Atlas) in the JRC workshop worked example: Mollaert & Stimpfle, 'CEN/TS 19102 Design of tensioned membrane structures', The second-generation Eurocodes workshop, 3-5 June 2025, slide 112 (γM 1.5 used, 'mat.: γM0 = 1.4, det.: γM2 = 1.5'; kbiax 1.00; kage 1.40; kdur,P 1.80; kdur,L 1.70; kdur,M 1.20; ktemp,70 2.00; ksize 1.00; situation 1 prestress fk/(γM kbiax kage kdur,P ktemp,70 ksize), situation 4 snow <= 1000 m fk/(γM kbiax kage kdur,M ksize), situation 5 wind fk/(γM kbiax kage ksize)). Single published source of prCEN values; the published TS Annex C.3 table was not accessible -> confirm against CEN/TS 19102:2023 Annex C and the NA

prestress_min.source: JRC132615 (2023) §3 quoting the TensiNet Design Guide [FM04] rule of thumb: 'for PVC coated polyester fabrics not less than 1.3% of the short term tensile strength', 'for PTFE coated glass fibre fabrics not less than 2.5% of the short term tensile strength, but not less than 2.0 kN/m'; French recommendations (Code Review No. 6): 'initial prestress of at least 1.5 kN/m'; practice 1.8-3.5 kN/m

fractile_kn.source: EN 1990 Annex D Table D1, 5 % fractile, Vx known, n -> infinity; fk,23 = n23·(1 − kn·Vx) as in JRC132615 eq. (6-1) and the JRC 2025 worked example (Vx 0.12 -> 0.803)

french_gamma_t.source: French recommendations (Code Review No. 21 in JRC132615): TD = kq·ke·Trm/γt, Table 6-2 γt = 4 (medium pollution) / 4.5 (heavy pollution) for polyester and glass fibre fabrics; Trm = mean uniaxial strength

french_kq_uncontrolled.source: French recommendations (JRC132615 Code Review No. 21): quality factor kq = min(kt, ks) = 1 with external-lab-validated self-control or ISO 9001, otherwise 0.8

french_ke_area_ref.source: French recommendations (JRC132615 Code Review No. 21) eq. (3a)/(3b): ke = 1 for S <= 50 m2, ke = (50/S)^(1/15) for S > 50 m2 (Table 6-1: 0.9 for 50-200 m2, 0.86 for 250-500 m2)

french_gamma_tloc.source: French recommendations (JRC132615 Code Review No. 21) eq. (4): attachment areas TD = kq·neff·Trm/γtloc, γtloc = 5; edges: safety factor >= 2.5 on the lowest of >= 3 edge tests

gamma_prestress.source: Eng. Struct. 214 (2020) calibration: gP=1.0 with gS=gW=2.0 (or gP=1.2 with 1.5)

gamma_variable.source: EN 1990 gQ; calibration study suggests 2.0 with gP=1.0

asce55_10_PD.source: ASCE 55-10 industry-practice FS for prestress + dead (consistent with FM DS 1-59)

tear_factor.source: no code value found; practice: design stress ≤ critical-slit (tear propagation) resistance / ≥ 2 — agree with the checking engineer; second search: codes check tensile strength only, tear strength treated as a material property (Han Bao et al. 2022, J. Ind. Textiles). 2026 search: JRC132615 §7.7 'Tear control' gives no factor ('The calculation of tear propagation using the methods of fracture mechanics ... is currently a topic of research'); CEN/TS 19102 §9.5 'Tear control' content not accessible. See membrane-fabric/reference/verification-log.md

etfe_gamma.source: JRC132615 (2023) Eurocode Outlook No. 44 (ETFE foil): 'The recommended value for foil structures is γM= 1.1'; also Moritz concept Table 6-7 γm,ULS = 1.1. Used with the characteristic elastic limit fy10%,23 and the k factors in etfe_k (design proposal; confirm against CEN/TS 19102 §8.3 / Annex C.5 and the NA)

etfe_k.source: JRC132615 (2023) Eurocode Outlook No. 44 recommended values (no project tests): kage 1.05, klong 1.2, kperm 1.8 (3.5 for single-layer foil with no regulation in the attachment details), ktemp0 0.7, ktemp50 1.2, ktemp70 1.7, fy10%,23 = 21 N/mm2; fPM,d = fy/(γM·kage·kperm), fLTL,d = fy/(γM·kage·klong·ktemp0), fLTR,d = fy/(γM·kage·klong), fST,d = fy/(γM·kage), fSTH,d = fy/(γM·kage·ktemp50); worked: 'fPM,d = 21 / (1.1 · 1.05 · 1.8) = 10.1 N/mm²'

rho_air.source: EN 1991-1-4 4.5(1) Note 2 recommended air density 1.25 kg/m³

added_mass_model.source: scale on the added air mass that membrane_check.py computes per panel (Rayleigh integral of the baffled flat rectangular panel, fundamental sine mode, per air side; C_a = 0.726 square, 0.704 for 2:1, 0.646 for 4:1, normalised by r_eq = sqrt(AB/π)). The same integral reproduces Lamb (1920) 0.6689 for the clamped circular plate and 8/(3π) for the rigid piston; circular membrane mode 0.746, consistent with Zhao & Yu (2012, World J. Mech. 2, Table 2) NAVMI rising from 0.654 (plate) to 0.739 at tension parameter 1e4. 1.0 = baffled panel (largest added mass -> lowest, conservative f)
added_mass_model.range_source: unbaffled isolated canopy: air flows round the edges; for the rigid disk the two-sided unbaffled added mass (8/3)ρa³ is half the baffled two-sided value (Lamb), so 0.5 is the lower bound; curvature and wind flow not covered

corner_ply_eff.source: load share of each welded reinforcement ply (linear model n_eff = 1 + (k−1)·η), used only with membrane_check.py --neff-basis eta. With η = 0.8 it gives n_eff 1.8 / 2.6 / 3.4 for 1 / 2 / 3 reinforcement plies; published n_eff tables are in reinforcement_neff
corner_ply_eff.range_source: JRC132615 §6.5: French recs 1.9/2.6/3.1 (η 0.9 then 0.7, 0.5), German practice 1.75/2.6 (η 0.75, 0.5×1.75), Eurocode Outlook 38 safe-sided 1.5 (η 0.5)

reinforcement_neff.source: JRC132615 (2023) §6.5 'Membrane reinforcement': French recommendations 'fabric + 1 reinforcement: neff = 1.9, + 2: 2.6, + 3: 3.1'; German practice 'one reinforcement layer calculated with 75%: neff = 1.75, second reinforcement layer calculated with 50%: neff = 1.75·1.5 = 2.6'; Eurocode Outlook No. 38 (CEN/TC 250 WG5 safe-sided): 'the design resistance is increased by 50% unless a more precise evaluation by tests has been performed. NOTE For more than 1 reinforcement layer tests have to be performed.' Lists index = total plies − 1

gammaR.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.2 (recommended, NDP): 'Measures to minimise bending stresses at the anchorage: Yes 0,90 / No 1,00'; ETAs (Fatzer ETA-15/0917, Pfeifer, Teufelberger-Redaelli ETA-18/1122) use 1.0; DIBt does not permit < 1.0. Stainless strand ETAs may use 1.1 (Carl Stahl ETA-10/0358 γM = 1.1; Redaelli OSX F_Rd = F_uk/1.65)

resistance_div.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text eq. (6.2): F_Rd = min{F_uk/(1,5 γR); F_k/γR}

ke_socket.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.3: 'Metal filled socket 1,0 / Resin filled socket 1,0'

ke_swaged.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.3: 'Swaged socket 0,9'. Product ETAs can be lower (Carl Stahl ETA-10/0358 stainless swaged: 0.9 (6–10 mm), 0.82 (12–14), 0.78 (1x61))

ke_ferrule.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.3: 'Ferrule-secured eye 0,9' (EN 13411-3 terminal)

ke_ubolt.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.3: 'U-bolt grip 0,8 *)  *) For U-bolt grip a reduction of preload is possible.' (EN 13411-5; not for primary members)

f_sls.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 7.2 (recommended, NA may change): 'Fatigue design without bending stresses 0,45 σuk'; 'Fatigue design including bending stresses 0,50 σuk'. NOTE 4: 0,45 σuk is used for testing (Annex A)
f_sls.range_source: not an uncertainty: the two Table 7.2 values; which one applies depends on whether the fatigue design includes bending stresses (use --bending-checked for 0.50)

alpha_carbon.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 3.3(1) eq. (3.1): αT = 12 x 10^-6 per °C for steel wires

alpha_stainless.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 3.3(1) eq. (3.1): αT = 16 x 10^-6 per °C for stainless steel wires

clamp_mu.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.4.1 defines μ but gives NO value: determine by slip test (Annex A). 0.1 is a conservative placeholder (also used with EN eq. (6.9) by Sun et al. 2025, Sci. Rep. 15, s41598-025-89571-3, https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-89571-3); T/CECS 1010-2022 'comprehensive friction coefficient ... outer bare sealing cable is 0.2' and JTG/T D65-05-2015 0.15 (both as quoted by Sun et al. 2025); Ruan 2019 (Adv. Civ. Eng. doi:10.1155/2019/1438754): cast-steel clamps 0.30–0.46
clamp_mu.range_source: below the placeholder … T/CECS 1010-2022 value 0.2 (bare sealing cable, per Sun et al. 2025)

clamp_gamma.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.4.1 NOTE 1: 'γM,fr = 1,65 is recommended' (same value for saddle slip, 6.3.2 NOTE). Check (6.9): F_Ed,∥ ≤ (F_Ed,⊥ + F_r)μ/γM,fr

clamp_preload_factor.source: EN 1993-1-8:2005 3.9.1(2) eq. (3.7): preloading force of class 8.8/10.9 bolts with controlled tightening F_p,C = 0,7·f_ub·A_s (full text); used for clamp bolts by cable_calc.py clamp

clamp_loss.source: retained fraction of the bolt preload in F_r. EN 1993-1-11:2006 6.3.2(3) lists the losses (creep, diameter reduction under tension, bedding/ovalisation, external forces, temperature) but gives no value. 0.8 assumes the bolts are re-tightened after stressing (SKILL rule). Without re-tightening the literature is much lower: T/CECS 1010-2022 'P_e = (1 − φ_B)P_0', 'φ_B ... take 0.25–0.55', and 'the loss rate of the initial tightening force of high-strength bolts is 49%' (both quoted by Sun et al. 2025, Sci. Rep., https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-89571-3)

saddle_p_lim_FLC.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.4 q_Rk (no tests), fully locked coil rope, steel clamps and saddles: 40 N/mm². Applies to the pressure from the radial clamping force F_r, q_Ed = F_r/(d'·L2) (6.8); 6.3.3 NOTE: the pressure from F_Ed is covered by the radius rules of 6.3.1

saddle_p_lim_OSS.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.4 q_Rk (no tests), spiral strand rope, steel clamps and saddles: 25 N/mm² (clamping pressure, see saddle_p_lim_FLC)

saddle_min_R_over_d.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.3.1(2): 'The radius r1 of the saddle should not be less than the greater of 30d or r1 ≥ 400⌀' (d cable, ⌀ wire); then wire curvature stresses may be neglected (Fig. 6.1 NOTE: breaking resistance reduced ≤ 3 %). 6.3.1(4): smaller radii for spiral ropes only where justified by tests

saddle_min_R_over_d_lined.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.3.1(3): 'r1 may be reduced to 20d when the bedding of the rope on at least 60% of the diameter is coated with soft metal or zinc spray with a minimum thickness of 1 mm'

saddle_min_R_over_wire.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.3.1(2): r1 ≥ 400⌀ (⌀ = wire diameter); the tool keeps it with a lining too (conservative reading of 6.3.1(3))

saddle_k.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.3.4(1) NOTE: saddles designed for k·F_uk, 'The value of k = 1,10 is recommended' (NDP)

saddle_k_clamp.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.3.2(2) eq. (6.7): k 'normally 2,0 where there is full friction developed between the saddle grooves and the clamp ... otherwise k = 1,0'

saddle_gamma_bed.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 6.3.3 Table 6.4 NOTE 1: 'The use of the limiting values qRk with γM,bed = 1,00 should lead to a reduction of not more than 3 % of the breaking strength' (γM,bed not given as an NDP value; NA may set one)

f_sls_bending_checked.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 7.2: 'Fatigue design including bending stresses 0,50 σuk' (recommended, NA may change)

f_const_install.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 7.1: 'First tension components for only a few hours 0,60 σuk'; 'After instalment of other tension components 0,55 σuk' (see f_const_after)

f_const_after.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 7.1: 'After instalment of other tension components 0,55 σuk'

saddle_p_lim_FLC_lined.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.4 q_Rk (no tests), fully locked coil rope, cushioned clamps and saddles (soft metal or sprayed zinc ≥ 1 mm, NOTE 2): 100 N/mm²

saddle_p_lim_OSS_lined.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 6.4 q_Rk (no tests), spiral strand rope, cushioned clamps and saddles: 60 N/mm²

creep_shortening_mm_per_m.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text 3.2.2(3) NOTE 1: 'In the absence of more accurate values this effect [creep of long cables vs short test samples] may be taken into account for cutting to length by applying an additional shortening of 0,15 mm/m'

k2_thread.source: EN 1993-1-8 Table 3.4 bolt tension k2 = 0.9 (0.63 countersunk); used for threaded tension rods on A_s

imp_alpha.source: EN 1993-1-1 Table 6.1 imperfection factors for buckling curves (also 6.3.2.2 Table 6.3 for LTB curves a-d)

e0_elastic.source: EN 1993-1-1 Table 5.1 design value of initial local bow imperfection e0/L, elastic analysis

phi0.source: EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(3)a basic global sway imperfection phi0 = 1/200 (before alpha_h, alpha_m)

alpha_cr_min_elastic.source: EN 1993-1-1 5.2.1(3) eq. (5.1): first-order analysis may be used if alpha_cr >= 10 (elastic analysis; 15 for plastic)

class_limits.source: EN 1993-1-1 Table 5.2 c/t limits for class 1/2/3 (multiplied by eps; CHS d/t by eps^2)

C1_end_moments.source: SCI/Access Steel NCCI SN003b-EN-EU Table 3.1 'Values of C1 for end moment loading (for k = 1)', psi = +1..-1: 1,00 1,14 1,31 1,52 1,77 2,05 2,33 2,57 2,55 (https://www.steelconstruction.info/images/0/0f/SN003b.pdf); values computed with kappa_wt = 0, 'conservative'

Cm_min.source: EN 1993-1-1 Annex B Table B.3 linear moment: Cm = 0.6 + 0.4 psi >= 0.4

Cm_sway.source: EN 1993-1-1 Annex B Table B.3 note: members with sway buckling mode Cmy = 0.9 (Cmz = 0.9)

gamma_G_stb.source: EN 1997-1 Table A.1 (EQU) stabilising permanent action

gamma_G_dst.source: EN 1997-1 Table A.1 (EQU) destabilising permanent action

gamma_Q_dst.source: EN 1997-1 Table A.1 (EQU) destabilising variable action

gamma_R_h.source: EN 1997-1 Table A.5 (spread foundations) R2 sliding resistance gamma_R;h = 1.1 (Design Approach 2)

gamma_G_sup.source: EN 1997-1 Table A.3 set A1 (= EN 1990 Table A1.2(B)) unfavourable permanent action, used for the bearing check (DA2)

gamma_G_inf.source: EN 1997-1 Table A.3 set A1 favourable permanent action, used for the bearing check (DA2)

gamma_conc.source: EN 1991-1-1 Table A.1 plain concrete ~24 kN/m3

helical_Kt_per_m.source: ICC-ES ESR-2794 (Hubbell CHANCE, reissued May 2026) sec. 4.1.5: 'Kt = Torque correlation factor of 10 ft-1 (32.8 m-1) for the CHANCE Model SS5 (1.5-inch) and SS175 (1.75-inch) square shaft piles' (https://www.icc-es.org/wp-content/uploads/report-directory/ESR-2794.pdf); default = square shaft

helical_FS.source: ICC-ES ESR-2794 sec. 4.1.5 eq. 4 'Qall = 0.5 Qult' and 'F.S. = an appropriate factor of safety for the project, not less than 2.0' (2.5 under the IRC without a geotechnical investigation); IBC 1810.3.3.1.9

k_ucr_N.source: EN 1992-4 7.2.1.4 cast-in headed fasteners, uncracked (Hilti, IDEA StatiCa, civilaxis)

gamma_Ms_steel.source: EN 1992-4 Table 4.1: γMs = 1.2·f_uk/f_yk ≥ 1.4 (computed per anchor grade)

6082T6_fo_thin.source: 6082-T6 extrusions t ≤ 5 mm f_o (EN 755-2 / EN 1999-1-1 Table 3.2b)

bearing_formula.source: EN 1999-1-1 Table 8.5 F_b,Rd = k1·αb·f_u·d·t/γM2 (EN 1993-1-8 form; EN 1999 table not quoted verbatim)

gMf_safe_life_high.source: EN 1993-1-9 Table 3.1 safe life, high consequence

gMf_safe_life_low.source: EN 1993-1-9 Table 3.1 safe life, low consequence

gMf_damage_tol_high.source: EN 1993-1-9 Table 3.1 damage tolerant, high consequence

gMf_damage_tol_low.source: EN 1993-1-9 Table 3.1 damage tolerant, low consequence

dsC_spiral_socket.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 9.1 (with Fig. 9.1): 'Fully locked coil rope with metal or resin socketing 150'; 'Spiral strands with metal or resin socketing 150' (exposure classes 3 and 4; valid only with Annex A sockets, 6 and 8 detailing, corrosion protection, 9.2(2)). Lower national practice: BASt hanger guideline Δσc = 112 N/mm² for full-locked hangers
dsC_spiral_socket.range_source: not an uncertainty in the EN value: BASt/German practice 112 (FLC hangers) … EN Table 9.1 150; prEN 1993-1-11 revises the FLC S-N curve (Steel Construction 2021, doi:10.1002/stco.202100009)

dsC_parallel_wire.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 9.1: 'Parallel wire strands with epoxy socketing 160'; 'Bundle of parallel strands 160'; 'Bundle of parallel wires 160'
dsC_parallel_wire.range_source: degenerate range (no evidence for another value); kept because fatigue_check.py --sensitivity reads it

dsC_threaded_bar.source: EN 1993-1-9:2005 full text Table 8.1 detail 14: 'Bolts and rods with rolled or cut threads in tension' category 50, Δσ on the tensile stress area; size effect for φ > 30 mm: ks = (30/φ)^0.25. (EN 1993-1-11 Table 9.1 gives 105 for prestressing bars, not for threaded tension rods)

dsC_prestressing_bar.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Table 9.1 group A: 'Prestressing bars 105'

m_rope.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Figure 9.1 (fatigue strength curves for tension components): slope m = 4 down to Δσc at 2×10^6 cycles, m = 6 beyond (see m2_rope, N_knee_rope); fatigue_check.py uses m = 4 for all N (conservative beyond 2×10^6)
m_rope.range_source: the two slopes of EN 1993-1-11 Fig. 9.1 (m = 4 for N ≤ 2×10^6, m = 6 beyond)

m2_rope.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Figure 9.1: second slope 1:6 beyond 2×10^6 cycles (no cut-off drawn)

N_knee_rope.source: EN 1993-1-11:2006 + AC:2009 full text Figure 9.1: knee of the tension-component curve at 2×10^6 cycles (= Δσc)

fabrication._note: patterning / shop-drawing thresholds used by fabrication-drawings tools (practice values, not code requirements unless status C/V)

flatten_strain_warn_pct.source: practice rule: flattening strain should stay well below the compensation values (0.3-0.5 %); no published numeric limit found (searched Dlubal RF-CUTTING-PATTERN, Warwick/TUM patterning papers) - project / fabricator to confirm
flatten_strain_warn_pct.range_source: 0.3-0.5 % rule of thumb (fabrication-drawings/reference/patterning.md); 1 % = typical lowest warp compensation of PVC fabrics

mating_seam_tol_mm_per_m.source: practice rule: compensated lengths of mating seams equal within about 1-2 mm/m (fabrication-drawings/reference/patterning.md); not from a standard
